We use a data sample collected with the BaBar detector at the PEP2 storage ring, corresponding to 232 million $B\bar B$ pairs. This study presents the first three-dimensional amplitude measurements of the decays \(B\to \psi(2S)K^*\) and \(B\to \chi_{c1}K^*\). It also provides an updated measurement of the \(B\to J/\psi K^*\) decay. The analysis is based on data collected with the BaBar detector at the PEP2 storage ring, corresponding to a sample of 232 million \(B\bar B\) pairs.

The results show that the longitudinal polarization fraction is larger in decays involving the \(J^{PC}=1^{++}\) \(\chi_{c1}\) meson than in those containing the \(J^{PC}=1^{--}\) charmonium states \(J/\psi\) or \(\psi(2S)\). In addition, the measurements reveal no evidence of direct \(CP\)-violating charge asymmetry in any of the studied decay modes.

A sample of approximately \(232\times10^{6}\) \(B\bar B\) pairs collected with the BaBar detector at the PEP-II asymmetric-energy \(e^+e^-\) collider is used to study the decays \(B\to(c\bar c)K^*\), where the charmonium state is \(J/\psi\), \(\psi(2S)\), or \(\chi_{c1}\). The analysis provides the first full three-dimensional angular measurements of the decay amplitudes in \(B\to\psi(2S)K^*\) and \(B\to\chi_{c1}K^*\), together with an updated and more precise measurement of \(B\to J/\psi K^*\).

Because both the charmonium state and the \(K^*\) carry spin, these decays can proceed through several helicity configurations. Their dynamics are described in terms of longitudinal, parallel-transverse, and perpendicular-transverse amplitudes. An unbinned fit to the three decay angles is used to determine the corresponding polarization fractions and relative phases, with detector acceptance, backgrounds, and cross-feed among reconstructed channels incorporated into the analysis. Charged and neutral \(B\) modes and their charge-conjugate decays are included.

The \(J/\psi K^*\) and \(\psi(2S)K^*\) channels exhibit broadly similar polarization patterns, as expected because both charmonium states have quantum numbers \(J^{PC}=1^{--}\). In contrast, the decay \(B\to\chi_{c1}K^*\), involving the axial-vector \(1^{++}\) state, is substantially more longitudinally polarized. The measured longitudinal fraction is about \(0.77\) for \(\chi_{c1}K^*\), compared with roughly one half for the two vector-charmonium modes. This difference indicates that the spin-parity structure of the charmonium state has an important influence on the helicity amplitudes and provides useful information for models of hadronic \(B\) decays and factorization.

The fitted phases also show that the polarization amplitudes are not all relatively real, pointing to non-negligible final-state interactions. Comparisons of the angular distributions and amplitudes for \(B\) and \(\bar B\) candidates reveal no statistically significant direct \(CP\)-violating charge asymmetry in any of the studied channels. Overall, the measurements establish the polarization structure of \(B\to\psi(2S)K^*\) and \(B\to\chi_{c1}K^*\) for the first time, improve the corresponding information for \(B\to J/\psi K^*\), and provide new tests of theoretical descriptions of exclusive charmonium production in \(B\)-meson decays.
outputs.L5:
## BaBar

BaBar, usually written **BABAR**, was a major particle-physics experiment conducted at the **SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory** in California. Its detector operated at the PEP-II electron–positron collider from 1999 to 2008.

The experiment was designed primarily to study differences between matter and antimatter, especially a phenomenon known as **CP violation** in B mesons. These short-lived particles were produced in large numbers when electrons and positrons collided. By comparing the decay patterns of B mesons and their antiparticles, BaBar helped confirm that CP violation could be explained largely by the Standard Model of particle physics.

BaBar also investigated many other subjects, including rare particle decays, charm physics, tau leptons, and possible evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model. Its results contributed to the work that led to the 2008 Nobel Prize in Physics for Makoto Kobayashi and Toshihide Maskawa.

The experiment’s name was inspired by the B meson and its antiparticle, written **B-bar**, while also playfully referring to Babar the Elephant. Although data collection has ended, scientists continue to use BaBar’s extensive archive for new analyses and precision measurements.

counterfactuals.prompt: What are the key experimental results from a three-dimensional analysis of \(B\to(c\bar c)K^*\) decays involving \(J/\psi\), \(\psi(2S)\), and \(\chi_{c1}\) mesons?
counterfactuals.output:
A three-dimensional transversity-angle fit to \(B\to(c\bar c)K^*(892)\) found the following polarization fractions:

\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
(c\bar c) & |A_0|^2 & |A_\parallel|^2 & |A_\perp|^2\\ \hline
J/\psi & 0.556\pm0.009\pm0.010 &
0.211\pm0.010\pm0.006 &
0.233\pm0.010\pm0.005\\
\psi(2S) & 0.48\pm0.05\pm0.02 &
0.22\pm0.06\pm0.02 &
0.30\pm0.06\pm0.02\\
\chi_{c1} & 0.77\pm0.07\pm0.04 &
0.20\pm0.07\pm0.04 &
0.03\pm0.04\pm0.02
\end{array}
\]

The main conclusions were:

- \(J/\psi K^*\) and \(\psi(2S)K^*\) have compatible polarization patterns, with substantial transverse and CP-odd components.
- \(\chi_{c1}K^*\) is markedly different: it is predominantly longitudinally polarized and has an \(A_\perp\) component consistent with zero.
- For \(J/\psi K^*\), the measured relative phases were approximately
  \[
  \delta_\parallel\simeq -2.93,\qquad \delta_\perp\simeq 2.91\ {\rm rad},
  \]
  with similarly large phases for \(\psi(2S)K^*\). Their departure from the naive \(0\) or \(\pi\) expectations indicates non-negligible final-state interactions.
- No significant differences between \(B\) and \(\bar B\) amplitudes were observed, so there was no evidence for direct CP violation.

The first uncertainty in the table is statistical and the second systematic.
